enbraçan: enbraçar — to take (the shield) on the arm by its straps (present 3rd pl.; enbraçan los escudos 'they take their shields on their arms'; = embrazan)
coraçones: coraçón — heart (pl.; de fuertes coraçones 'with stout hearts'; = corazones)
abaxan: abaxar — to lower (present 3rd pl.; abaxan las lanças 'they lower their lances'; = bajan; modern abajar survives only as a rare, dialectal word)
abueltas: a bueltas de — together with, along with (adverbial phrase, a + bueltas 'turns', from bolver; abueltas de los pendones 'together with the pennons'; the el is Pidal's restoration; = a vueltas de, junto con)
enclinaron: enclinar — to bend, incline (preterite 3rd pl.; enclinaron las caras 'they bent their faces (down)'; = inclinaron)
suso: suso — up, above (adverb, Latin sursum; de suso de los arzones 'above the saddle-bows'; no modern equivalent, closest arriba)
arzones: arzón — saddle-bow, the raised front or back of the saddle (pl.; = arzones)
ívanlos: ir + los — iban 'they were going' (imperfect 3rd pl.) + los 'them' (object pronoun split out); ir + infinitive, 'were going to, set about' (ívanlos ferir 'they went to strike them'; = los iban a herir)
llama: llamar — he calls, cries out (present 3rd sg.; A grandes vozes llama 'he calls at the top of his voice'; = llama)
feridlos: ferir + los — ferid 'strike!' (imperative 2nd pl.) + los 'them' (object pronoun split out); = heridlos
fieren: ferir — they strike, attack (present 3rd pl.; fieren en el az 'they strike into the line'; = hieren)
seños: seños — one each (distributive, plural only; Latin singulos; seños moros 'a Moor apiece'; de seños colpes 'with one blow each'; = sendos)
tornada: tornada — turn, return, wheeling back (noun, from tornar; a la tornada 'on the return (charge)'; = vuelta)
tantos: tanto — so many (masc. pl.; tantos pendones 'so many pennons'; a la tornada … otros tantos 'as many more'; = tantos)
tantas: tanto — so many (fem. pl.; tantas lanças 'so many lances'; = tantas)
premer: premer — to press down, lower (infinitive, Latin premere; premer e alçar 'to lower and raise' the lances; no modern simple verb, cf. apremiar, oprimir, closest apretar)
tanta: tanto — so many, so much (fem. sg. used collectively; tanta adágara 'so many a shield'; = tanta)
adágara: adágara — small round or heart-shaped shield, buckler (word of Arabic origin, ad-daraqa; = adarga)
foradar: foradar — to pierce, bore through (infinitive, Latin forare; adágara foradar 'to pierce shields'; = horadar)
loriga: loriga — coat of mail, hauberk (= loriga, now only a historical term; cota de malla is the usual word)
desmanchar: desmanchar — to break the mail of (a hauberk) (infinitive; Pidal 'desmallar', to break the links or plates of the hauberk; loriga falssar e desmanchar 'hauberks pierced and their mail broken'; = desmallar)
blancos: blanco — white (masc. pl.; pendones blancos 'white pennons'; = blancos)
salir: salir — to come out, emerge (infinitive; salir vermejos en sangre 'to come out red with blood'; = salir)
mafómat: Mafómat — Muhammad, the Moors' battle-cry (llaman Mafómat 'they call on Muhammad'; = Mahoma)
santi: santi — saint (old form before a saint's name, from Latin sancti as in Sancti Iacobi, which survives fused in Santiago; santi Yagüe 'Saint James'; = santo, san)
yagüe: Yagüe — James, Iago (from Latin Iacobus; santi Yagüe = Santiago, Saint James, patron of Spain and the Christians' battle-cry; = Yago, Jacobo, in Santiago)
cadien: caer (old cader, Latin cadere) — they were falling (imperfect 3rd pl., -ié ending; = caían)
quál: quál — how, what a (exclamative; ¡quál lidia bien! 'how well he fights!'; = cuál, here cómo)
lidia: lidiar — he fights (present 3rd sg.; = lidia, closest lucha)
exorado: exorado — gilded, adorned with gold (adj., Latin exauratus; arzón exorado 'gilded saddle-bow'; probably so; no modern equivalent, closest dorado)
arzón: arzón — saddle-bow (sg.; sobre exorado arzón 'upon the gilded saddle-bow', i.e. in the saddle; = arzón)
diaz: Díaz — Díaz (patronymic 'son of Diego'; Ruy Diaz, the Cid's name, = Ruy Díaz; same as díaz, here without accent)
çorita: Çorita — Zorita, the place held by Minaya (que Çorita mandó 'who held Çorita'); Pidal finds Álvar Fáñez as lord of Zorita in documents of 1097 and 1107 — taken to be Zorita de los Canes on the Tagus (Guadalajara)
muño: Muño — personal name (Muño Gustioz, a vassal of the Cid; = Munio, an old name; Nuño is probably related)
gustioz: Gustioz — patronymic 'son of Gustio' (Muño Gustioz, the Cid's retainer, brought up in his household; = Gustioz, no modern form)
criado: criado — one brought up in a lord's household, foster-son, retainer (past part. of criar used as noun; so criado 'his foster-son, reared in his house'; modern criado = servant)
martin: Martín — Martín (personal name; Martin Muñoz, governor of Mont Mayor; same as martín, here without accent)
muñoz: Muñoz — patronymic 'son of Muño' (Martín Muñoz, Félez Muñoz; = Muñoz)
mont: Mont — mount, hill (Latin montem; = monte); Mont Mayor, the place Martín Muñoz held: Montemayor, a Portuguese town he governed for Alfonso VI, according to Pidal
albaroz: Albaroz — patronymic 'son of Álvaro/Álbar' (Álbar Albaroz = Álvar Álvarez; = Álvarez)
aragón: Aragón — Aragon, the kingdom/region east of Castile (el bueno de Aragón 'the good (man) from Aragon'; = Aragón)
félez: Félez — personal name, Félez Muñoz, nephew of the Cid; the name is probably from Latin Felix (= Félix; Félez is not a modern name)
sobrino: sobrino — nephew (= sobrino; so sobrino 'his nephew')
adelante: adelante — onward, further on (adverb; desí adelante 'from there on, further'; = adelante)
acorren: acorrer — they come to help, rush to aid (present 3rd pl.; acorren la seña 'rally to the banner'; bien lo acorren 'they help him well'; = socorren, acuden a; modern acorrer is archaic)
matáronle: matar + le — mataron 'they killed' (preterite 3rd pl.) + le dative of possession 'on him' (matáronle el cavallo 'they killed his horse under him'; = le mataron el caballo)
quebrada: quebrar — broken (past part., fem. sg., agreeing with lança; la lança a quebrada 'he has broken the lance'; = quebrada, rota)
metió: meter — he put (preterite 3rd sg.; metió mano 'laid hand to'; = metió)
víolo: veer + lo — vio 'he saw' (preterite 3rd sg.) + lo 'it, him' (object pronoun split out; = lo vio)
acostós: acostar + se — acostó 'he approached' (preterite 3rd sg.) + se (reflexive; acostarse a 'to draw up beside'; modern acostarse means 'to lie down', so = se acercó)
aguazil: aguazil — Moorish officer, vizier or commander (Arabic al-wazīr; here a Moorish chief; = alguacil, modern 'bailiff, constable')
tenié: tener — he had, was mounted on (imperfect 3rd sg., -ié ending; que tenié buen cavallo 'who had a good horse'; = tenía)
diol: dar + le — dio 'he gave' (preterite 3rd sg.) + l(e) 'to him' (enclitic; diol tal espadada 'gave him such a sword-stroke'; = le dio)
espadada: espadada — sword-stroke, blow with a sword (noun; = espadazo)
cortól: cortar + le — cortó 'he cut' (preterite 3rd sg.) + l(e) 'him' (enclitic; = le cortó)
ival: ir + le — iva 'he was going' (imperfect 3rd sg.) + l(e) 'to him'; ir + infinitive 'was about to' (ival dar el cavallo 'he was going to give him the horse'; = le iba a dar)
abré: aver — I shall have (future 1st sg., syncopated; de vos abré grand bando 'from you I shall have great support'; = habré)
bando: bando — party, side, backing (Germanic word; abré grand bando 'I shall have great support'; modern bando = faction, also proclamation)
cometamos: cometer — let us attack (present subjunctive 1st pl., after a menester que 'it is necessary that'; cometer 'to attack'; modern cometer means 'to commit', so closest acometer, acometamos)
fuerças: fuerça — force, might; pl. forces, strong troops (por estas fuerças 'through these forces', i.e. among these hosts; = fuerzas)
alcança: alcançar — he overtakes, catches (present 3rd sg.; a los que alcança 'those whom he overtakes'; = alcanza)
valos: ir + los — va 'he goes' (present 3rd sg.) + los 'them'; ir + gerund 'goes on doing' (valos delibrando 'he goes on dispatching them'; = los va librando, despachando)
delibrando: delibrar — dispatching, killing (gerund; Pidal 'despachar, matar'; from Latin de + liberare; modern deliberar means 'to deliberate', so closest despachando, matando)
fallen: fallir — they fail, miss (present 3rd pl. of fallir 'to fail', not hallar 'to find'; los dos le fallen 'two of them miss him'; = fallan)
únol: uno + le — uno 'one' + l(e) 'him' (el únol ha tomado 'the one has caught him'; = el uno le)
tomado: tomar — taken, caught, hit (past part.; ha tomado 'has caught (him)'; = tomado)
bolvió: bolver — he turned (preterite 3rd sg.; bolvió la rienda 'he turned his rein'; = volvió)
írsele: ir + se + le — ir 'to go' (infinitive) + se (reflexive: irse 'to go away') + le (dative 'from him', 'on him'); por írsele del campo 'so as to slip away from the field'; = para irse
rancado: rancar — routed, driven off (past part., = arrancado; Old Spanish rancar 'to pull out, uproot', here 'to rout'; rancado es el fonssado 'the host is routed'; modern rancar does not exist in this sense)
fonssado: fonssado — army, host (Latin fossatum 'ditch, entrenched camp'; in medieval Castile also a military expedition and the service owed for it; rancar el fonssado, Pidal 'vencer al ejército'; = hueste, ejército)
dio: dar — he gave, struck (preterite 3rd sg.; un colpe dio 'he struck a blow'; = dio)
carbonclas: carbonclas — carbuncles, red gems set in the helmet as ornament (fem. pl., from Latin carbunculus; Pidal 'carbunclos' o rubíes; = carbunclos, carbúnculos)
echógelas: echar + ge + las — echó 'he threw' (preterite 3rd sg.) + ge (= le 'to him', before an object pronoun; = se) + las 'them' (the carbuncles); echógelas aparte 'he knocked them off aside'; = se las echó
gel: ge + lo — ge (= le 'to him'; = se) + l(o) 'it' (non gel osó esperar 'did not dare wait for it (a second blow)'; probably so; = se lo)
esperar: esperar — to wait for, await, withstand (infinitive; non gel osó esperar 'did not dare to wait for it'; = esperar)
arrancado: arrancado — routed, driven off (past part. of arrancar, 'to pull out, uproot', here 'to rout'; arrancado es el rey 'the king is routed'; = arrancado, derrotado)
cristiandad: cristiandad — Christendom, the Christian people (= cristiandad; tan buen día por la cristiandad 'such a good day for Christendom')
della: de + ella — 'from/of her/it' (contraction); della e della part, 'from the one and the other side', i.e. from all sides (= de ella, here de una y otra parte)
alcaz: alcaz — pursuit, chase (verbal noun of alcançar; en alcaz 'in pursuit'; modern alcance means 'reach', closest persecución)
cogieron: coger — they took in, received, admitted (preterite 3rd pl.; nol cogieron allá 'did not take him in there'; modern coger means 'to take, catch', here = acogieron)
para: para — toward, to (para Cataluyuth 'toward Calatayud'; = para)
cataluyuth: Cataluyuth — Calatayud, the same name as Calatayuth with two syllables transposed (th is a spelling of final -d; the t is Pidal's restoration); = Calatayud
íval: ir + le — iva 'he was going' (imperfect 3rd sg.) + l(e) 'him, after him' (íval en alcaz 'he went after him in pursuit'; = le iba)
segudar: segudar — to pursue (infinitive; Pidal 'perseguir'; used as a noun, el segudar 'the pursuit'; no modern segudar, = perseguir, as a noun persecución)

__broaden__.de: de — of, from · also de — by (the agent with a passive participle; = por) · also de — 'by (night)' (de noch), partitive 'of, among' (quinze moros … de los que alcançava; pocas de gentes), 'as' (de ganançia 'as booty'), 'from outside' (de fuera), 'on the right' (de diestro) · also 'about, concerning' (de mí non digan mal 'let them not speak ill of me') · also de — 'as if in' (commo de arrancada 'as if in rout'); 'in the manner of' (de guisa 'in such a way'); 'of, among' (de bivos pocos 'of the living few'); nominalized infinitive (del prender 'of the taking') · also de — 'with' of manner (de fuertes coraçones 'with stout hearts'); 'on' (de pie 'on foot'); 'from' of side (della e della part 'from both sides'); de cabo 'anew' (de + cabo, 'again'); de suso de 'above'; seños … de seños colpes 'with one blow each'
__broaden__.a: a — to, at · also aver — he/she has (3rd sg. present, h-less spelling of ha, as in el rey me a ayrado = el rey me ha airado) · personal a before a direct object (salvest a Jonás; a ti adoro); a + inf. 'to, about to' (tornólas a catar); a tan grand sabor 'with so great pleasure'; a ojo 'in plain sight' · also a — 'into' (sacar a çelada 'to lure into ambush'); 'at, in' (a la çaga 'at the rear'); 'against' (dar salto a la çaga); dative 'to' (a mí dedes); haber a + inf. 'have to' (lo han a far); a + noun of direction (adeliñava a la puerta 'made for the gate') · impersonal 'there is' (aver; es dia a de plazo 'there is (only) a day of the term', the most likely reading of a hard line); ha as auxiliary set after the participle (soñado a 'he has dreamt') · also 'on, at (a time)' (a tercer dia 'on the third day') · also a — 'has' before the participle, agreeing with the object (la lança a quebrada 'he has broken the lance'; a menester 'has need of'); a + dative of the person affected (a Minaya matáronle el cavallo 'they killed Minaya's horse')
__broaden__.mandó: mandar — he ordered (preterite 3rd sg.; = mandó) · also mandar — 'he held, governed' a place (Çorita mandó 'he held Çorita'; el que mandó a Mont Mayor 'he who governed Mont Mayor')
__broaden__.mayor: mayor — larger, greater (aquella mayor az 'that greatest line'; = mayor) · also Mayor — part of the place name Mont Mayor, Montemayor (the Portuguese town, Pidal)
__broaden__.passar: passar — to cross, pass over (infinitive; = pasar) · also passar — 'to pass through, pierce' (tanta adágara foradar e passar 'so many shields pierced and passed through')
__broaden__.firme: firme — firm; used adverbially, 'firmly, securely' (= firmemente) · also firme' — firmes, 'firm, steadfast' (adjective plural, final s dropped; firme' son los moros 'the Moors are firm', i.e. still holding their ground)
__broaden__.nos: nos — we (subject pronoun; = nosotros) · also nos — us, to us (object pronoun; atorgar nos hedes 'you will grant us') · also reflexive 'ourselves' (nos partimos 'we part'); dative (la missa nos dirá 'will say for us') · also nos' — non + se (aun nos' van del campo 'they are still not leaving the field'; the apostrophe marks the elision)
__broaden__.cabo: cabo — beside, next to (preposition; cf. modern cabe) · also cabo — end (noun; fasta cabo del año, 'until the end of the year') · also de cabo — 'again, anew' (que los cometamos de cabo 'that we attack them again'; = de nuevo)
__broaden__.avié: aver — he had (imperfect of aver = haber, here a full verb 'to have, hold') · also impersonal 'there was' (mucho avié grant plaça 'there was a very great space'; = había) · also avié — auxiliary 'had' + participle, pluperfect (avié dado 'he had given'; = había dado)
__broaden__.dado: dado — gift, present (noun; Latin datum) · also dar — given, dealt (past part.; tres colpes le avié dado 'he had dealt him three blows'; = dado)
__broaden__.castellano: castellano — Castilian, of Castile (el Castellano, epithet of Alfonso as king of Castile; = castellano) · also el Castellano — an epithet of the Cid himself (mio Çid Roy Díaz el Castellano 'the Castilian')
__broaden__.diestro: diestro — right (hand, side), noun use (de diestro 'on the right'; = diestro, closest derecha) · also diestro — adjective 'right' (so diestro braço 'his right arm'); mio diestro braço 'my right arm', figuratively my chief support
__broaden__.medio: medio — middle; en medio de 'in the middle of' · also medio — 'the half' (noun; el medio echó en campo 'he threw the half onto the field'; = la mitad)
